what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from El Salvador in all host countries combined: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 108289 asylum seekers from El Salvador.
The United States hosts the largest share, 88.6%, followed by Mexico, Italy and Spain.

why.text: The fact pack records no armed conflict and no dated events for El Salvador, so it does not say why people left.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2000 to 2004 and 2017 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series starts in 2000 at its highest point, 176478 asylum seekers.
The figure fell to a low in 2010 and then rose again in the following years.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took.
These are year-end totals of asylum seekers summed over every host country; refugees from El Salvador are counted separately.
